tasks.title: Injection vulnerabilities
tasks.scope: Detect SQL injection, command injection, code injection, and template injection vulnerabilities in user-controlled input flows.
tasks.prompt: Inspect changed code for user-controlled inputs flowing into SQL queries, shell commands, eval constructs, template engines, or dynamic code execution without proper sanitization or parameterization. Trace data flow from entry points through processing layers to execution sinks. Research current framework-specific injection defense patterns using public documentation when framework usage is detected. Require concrete evidence linking changed lines to unsafe sink usage. Exclude findings when sanitization, parameterization, or framework protections are correctly applied. Do not report findings from other vulnerability classes. When repository technology stack is unclear, inspect import statements, dependency manifests, and runtime configuration to infer the environment before assessing defenses. Do not send repository code or file paths to web tools.
evidenceRequirements: Changed line range showing user input entering an unsafe sink
Data flow path from input source to execution point
Public framework or library documentation demonstrating unsafe usage pattern when framework-specific
Absence of parameterization, prepared statements, or escape functions at the sink
outOfScope: Authentication and authorization bypass (owned by access-control-vulnerabilities)
Cryptographic implementation flaws (owned by cryptographic-vulnerabilities)
Dependency vulnerabilities in third-party packages (owned by dependency-vulnerabilities)
Secrets and credentials exposure (owned by secrets-exposure)
Resource exhaustion or denial-of-service conditions (owned by resource-handling-vulnerabilities)
Style, formatting, or code quality issues unrelated to injection risk

tasks.title: Access control vulnerabilities
tasks.scope: Detect broken authentication, authorization bypass, privilege escalation, and insecure direct object references.
tasks.prompt: Inspect changed code for missing authentication checks, inadequate authorization validation, privilege escalation paths, and insecure direct object references. Trace request flows from entry points through permission checks to protected resources. Research current framework authentication and authorization patterns using public documentation when framework usage is detected. Require concrete evidence linking changed lines to bypassed or missing access controls. Exclude findings when proper role checks, ownership validation, or framework guard mechanisms are correctly applied. Do not report injection, cryptographic, or resource handling issues. When repository access control model is unclear, inspect middleware, decorators, route guards, and configuration to infer the protection strategy before reporting gaps. Do not send repository code or file paths to web tools.
evidenceRequirements: Changed line range showing protected resource access without authentication or authorization check
Control flow path demonstrating bypass or missing validation
Public framework or library documentation showing expected access control pattern when framework-specific
Absence of role validation, ownership check, or permission enforcement at the access point
outOfScope: Injection vulnerabilities in input handling (owned by injection-vulnerabilities)
Cryptographic implementation flaws (owned by cryptographic-vulnerabilities)
Dependency vulnerabilities in third-party packages (owned by dependency-vulnerabilities)
Secrets and credentials exposure (owned by secrets-exposure)
Resource exhaustion or denial-of-service conditions (owned by resource-handling-vulnerabilities)
Logging or monitoring gaps unrelated to access control enforcement

tasks.title: Cryptographic vulnerabilities
tasks.scope: Detect weak cryptographic algorithms, insecure random number generation, hardcoded keys, improper certificate validation, and insecure protocol usage.
tasks.prompt: Inspect changed code for usage of weak hashing algorithms, insecure encryption modes, predictable random number generators, hardcoded cryptographic keys, disabled certificate validation, and deprecated TLS versions. Trace cryptographic operations from initialization through usage. Research current cryptographic best practices and deprecated algorithm lists using public security guidance when specific libraries or protocols are detected. Require concrete evidence linking changed lines to insecure cryptographic choices. Exclude findings when modern algorithms, secure modes, proper key management, and strong randomness sources are used. Do not report injection, access control, or dependency issues. When repository cryptographic requirements are unclear, inspect security configuration, library choices, and protocol negotiation to infer the threat model before flagging outdated practices. Do not send repository code or file paths to web tools.
evidenceRequirements: Changed line range showing weak algorithm, insecure mode, or hardcoded key usage
Public security guidance or standards document identifying the algorithm or practice as insecure
Absence of modern replacement or secure configuration at the usage site
Cryptographic operation context showing sensitive data protection or authentication reliance
outOfScope: Injection vulnerabilities in input handling (owned by injection-vulnerabilities)
Authentication and authorization bypass (owned by access-control-vulnerabilities)
Dependency vulnerabilities in third-party packages (owned by dependency-vulnerabilities)
Secrets and credentials exposure in source or configuration (owned by secrets-exposure)
Resource exhaustion or denial-of-service conditions (owned by resource-handling-vulnerabilities)
Performance optimization or algorithm efficiency unrelated to security

tasks.title: Secrets exposure
tasks.scope: Detect hardcoded credentials, API keys, tokens, and sensitive configuration in source code, configuration files, and logs.
tasks.prompt: Inspect changed code and configuration for hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys, database credentials, and other secrets committed to source control or logged in plaintext. Scan string literals, configuration values, environment variable defaults, and logging statements. Research current secret management patterns and tool usage using public documentation when secret stores or environment injection systems are detected. Require concrete evidence linking changed lines to exposed secret values. Exclude findings when secrets are properly externalized through environment variables, secret stores, or encrypted vaults. Do not report injection, access control, or cryptographic algorithm issues. When repository secret management strategy is unclear, inspect configuration loading, environment variable usage, and deployment scripts to infer the approach before reporting exposure. Do not send detected secret values or repository code to web tools.
evidenceRequirements: Changed line range showing hardcoded credential, key, or token pattern
Pattern match or entropy analysis indicating high-confidence secret detection
Public documentation or tool guidance showing proper externalization pattern when applicable
Absence of secret store reference, environment variable injection, or encrypted vault usage
outOfScope: Injection vulnerabilities in input handling (owned by injection-vulnerabilities)
Authentication and authorization logic flaws (owned by access-control-vulnerabilities)
Cryptographic algorithm or mode selection (owned by cryptographic-vulnerabilities)
Dependency vulnerabilities in third-party packages (owned by dependency-vulnerabilities)
Resource exhaustion or denial-of-service conditions (owned by resource-handling-vulnerabilities)
Non-sensitive configuration values, feature flags, or public constants

tasks.title: Dependency vulnerabilities
tasks.scope: Detect known vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies, outdated packages, and insecure dependency configuration.
tasks.prompt: Inspect changed dependency manifests, lock files, and dependency installation configuration for packages with known CVEs, outdated versions with security patches, and insecure dependency sources. Cross-reference package names and versions against public vulnerability databases when specific dependencies are added or updated. Research current package security advisories and ecosystem-specific vulnerability disclosure channels using public sources. Require concrete evidence linking changed dependency versions to published CVEs or security advisories. Exclude findings when dependencies are current or patches are not yet available. Do not report application code vulnerabilities covered by other tasks. When repository dependency ecosystem is unclear, inspect manifest file formats and package manager configuration to identify the platform before querying vulnerability sources. Do not send repository code or file paths to web tools; use only public package names and versions.
evidenceRequirements: Changed dependency manifest or lock file line showing package name and version
Public CVE identifier, security advisory, or vulnerability database entry for the specific version
Availability of patched version or documented mitigation
Severity classification from public vulnerability disclosure
outOfScope: Injection vulnerabilities in application code (owned by injection-vulnerabilities)
Authentication and authorization logic in application code (owned by access-control-vulnerabilities)
Cryptographic implementation in application code (owned by cryptographic-vulnerabilities)
Secrets exposure in application configuration (owned by secrets-exposure)
Resource handling in application code (owned by resource-handling-vulnerabilities)
Dependency update recommendations without published security impact
License compliance or supply chain provenance unrelated to vulnerability disclosure

tasks.title: Resource handling vulnerabilities
tasks.scope: Detect resource exhaustion, denial-of-service conditions, unbounded loops, memory leaks, and missing input size limits.
tasks.prompt: Inspect changed code for unbounded resource consumption, missing request size limits, algorithmic complexity vulnerabilities, uncontrolled recursion, memory leaks, and file descriptor exhaustion. Trace resource allocation from input through processing to cleanup. Research current framework and runtime resource limit patterns using public documentation when specific platforms are detected. Require concrete evidence linking changed lines to resource exhaustion vectors. Exclude findings when proper limits, timeouts, pagination, and cleanup are implemented. Do not report injection, access control, or cryptographic issues. When repository deployment environment is unclear, inspect configuration, middleware, and runtime settings to infer resource constraints before reporting unbounded behavior. Do not send repository code or file paths to web tools.
evidenceRequirements: Changed line range showing unbounded resource allocation, missing limit, or cleanup gap
Control flow or data flow path demonstrating exhaustion vector
Public framework or runtime documentation showing expected limit or protection pattern when applicable
Absence of size limits, timeouts, circuit breakers, or resource cleanup at the vulnerable point
outOfScope: Injection vulnerabilities in input handling (owned by injection-vulnerabilities)
Authentication and authorization bypass (owned by access-control-vulnerabilities)
Cryptographic implementation flaws (owned by cryptographic-vulnerabilities)
Secrets and credentials exposure (owned by secrets-exposure)
Dependency vulnerabilities in third-party packages (owned by dependency-vulnerabilities)
Performance optimization or efficiency improvements without security impact
Logging volume or monitoring overhead unrelated to resource exhaustion risk

externalSources.title: RFC 8996: Deprecating TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1

missingInputs: Data sensitivity classification: which data requires cryptographic protection (PII, credentials, tokens) vs. non-sensitive data (public metadata, cache keys). Would improve severity calibration for hash function findings.
Deployment environment: cloud KMS usage (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), hardware security modules, secure enclaves. Would improve remediation recommendations for key management.
Regulatory requirements: FIPS 140-2/3, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR cryptographic mandates. Would affect severity levels (critical for regulated data).
Threat model: whether attackers can intercept network traffic (affects TLS severity), extract keys from source code (affects hardcoded key severity), or access encrypted data at rest.
Algorithm purpose context: whether specific MD5/SHA-1 usage is for cryptographic (vulnerable) or non-cryptographic (acceptable) purposes. Skill must infer from variable names and data-flow analysis.
Post-quantum migration strategy: timeline for adopting ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA; hybrid crypto requirements; RSA/ECDSA sunset date. Would inform whether to flag RSA-2048+ or ECDSA P-256+ as weak.
